candidate: MB-009 Korea Apartment Fee Spike Explainer
wedge: K-apt monthly public fee history + same-complex year-over-year baseline + peer-complex benchmark + category decomposition => answer the consumer question '왜 이번 달 관리비가 뛰었지?' with ranked drivers and whether the jump is building-specific or seasonal/market-wide, rather than another raw management-fee comparison site
last_material_result: One bounded pain-led discovery unit selected MB-009. The underlying pain is material and recurring: January 2026 nationwide apartment management fees were reported at KRW3,343/m², +4.3% YoY, with heating up about 13%, creating consumer 'bill shock' questions. Public K-apt-derived data is broad enough for a stateless/indexable product. However, the generic comparison layer is already crowded: K-apt itself offers comparisons and independent sites such as 관리비알리미 and billnono already aggregate tens of thousands of complexes and item-level averages. Therefore the candidate survives only as an explanation/anomaly wedge: automatically decompose a monthly spike into category contributions, compare against the same complex last year and peers, and label likely seasonal vs building-specific drivers. This is materially different from 'is my fee high?' but still needs a direct competitor/query-gap check before BUILD consideration.
economics: KRW0 research spend. Core data can be public/free and output can be stateless/indexable. Monetization would be ads plus adjacent moving/home-service affiliate or portfolio cross-promotion; direct payment is unlikely. Maintenance could stay low if monthly K-apt ingestion is automatable, but expected contribution is unproven and incumbent SEO strength is a meaningful acquisition risk.
next_checkpoint: Next run: test three materially different search/distribution wedges around 아파트 관리비 왜 올랐지, 관리비 전년 대비, and 단지별 관리비 급등/이상치. Check whether incumbents already provide automatic category-contribution explanations rather than tables. KILL if explanation intent is too weak or incumbents already answer it programmatically; otherwise validate K-apt data-access/update burden and indexable page architecture.
recommendation: KEEP at ASSESS for one competition/query-gap round only. Do not build a generic management-fee comparison site; that space is already served. Advance only if the automated 'why did it jump?' decomposition has a defensible search/action gap and can run with bounded monthly ingestion.
